1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3 d5 4.Bf4 Bg7 5.e3.name: Grünfeld Defence: Brinckmann Attack, Grünfeld Gambit

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3 d5 4.Bf4 Bg7 5.e3.strategy: Declines the gambit and puts the rook on the c-file, where it will look down the file when the position opens. White keeps the bishop on f4 and the pawn on e3 solid and avoids the sharp line in which Black's pieces come alive for the pawn on c7.
1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3 d5 4.Bf4 Bg7 5.e3.name: Grünfeld Defence: Brinckmann Attack, Grünfeld Gambit, Capablanca Variation

1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3 d5 4.Bf4 Bg7 5.e3.strategy: Accepts the gambit. After the trades on d5 the queen recaptures and c7 hangs, so White wins a pawn. In return Black develops with tempo and pushes against the d4 pawn, so White has to defend accurately rather than attack.

The natural recapture: the knight reaches the centre and attacks both the bishop on f4 and the knight on c3. Black accepts that a queen recapture on d5 will leave c7 unguarded: that is the pawn Black has offered.

The standard counter-strike: Black hits d4 at once, before White has settled. If White takes on c5, the position opens and Black's pieces get active play against the c3 knight; if White holds d4, Black can trade the central pawn and free the bishop on g7.
